turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the data

**1. The dominant signal is the process route, not the chemistry.**
Sorting by `target` reveals three clear regimes:

| Regime | Signature | target |
|---|---|---|
| As-rolled / normalized only (THT=30, TT=30) | no heat treatment | 225–275 |
| Through-hardened + high tempering (THT≈825–865, TT≈550–650) | Q&T | 325–650 |
| Carburized (NT=930, THT=30, **CT=930**, Ct=90–540, DT≈850–896, Dt=15–70, QmT=60–140, **TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5**) | case hardening + low-temp temper | **838–1190** |

Every sample above 830 MPa (except the 0.6 C / 2 % Si spring steels at ~740–930) belongs to the carburizing route. So the recipe must be: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930 (max), a real diffusion step (DT≈850–896, Dt≈15–70), quench, then a **low** temper (TT≈160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5).

**2. Within the carburized block, chemistry ranking.**
Two high-performing alloy families appear:
- High-Ni: Ni≈1.62–1.69, Cr≈0.45–0.59, Mo≈0.16–0.21 → 1034, 1054, 1056, 1082, 1124, **1190**
- High-Cr: Cr≈1.14–1.17, Ni≈0.04–0.06, Mo≈0.17 → 1068, 1074, 1080, 1104, 1120, 1144

Both plateaus are similar; the Ni–Cr–Mo family contains the single best point and its neighbours are uniformly ≥1030, i.e. a **broad** plateau (Ct from 140→540, Dt from 15→70, QmT 60→140 all still give 1030–1190). The Cr-only family collapses more if Cr drifts (Cr must sit near 1.15, its upper edge → not robust to +5%). Hence I pick Ni≈1.65, Cr≈0.58, Mo≈0.18 — both elements sit mid-range, so ±5% moves stay inside well-sampled territory.

**3. Core carbon must stay low (0.17–0.23)** — carburized grades; C=0.21 is central, ±5% (0.20–0.22) is fully covered. Si 0.28–0.35, Mn 0.51–0.81, Cu 0.05–0.14, P/S low (best points have P≤0.015, S≈0.012–0.019). RedRatio 440–860 all give >1030; 690 is central. Inclusion ratings dA≈0.05, dB≈0.005, dC≈0.004 are typical of the top rows and near-insensitive.

**4. Robustness check (±5 % single-variable).**
- NT, CT, Tt are at the upper bound (930, 930, 120) — the only observed high-strength setting; –5 % (883, 883, 114) still lies in the carburizing regime, and +5 % clips to the bound.
- Ct 500 → 475–525: all inside the 470–540 band that produced 1082–1190.
- DT 855 → 812–898, Dt 16 → 15.2–16.8, QmT 140 → 133–147, TT 165 → 157–173: all within observed high-strength ranges.
- Ni 1.65→1.57–1.73, Cr 0.58→0.55–0.61, Mo 0.18→0.171–0.189, C 0.21→0.20–0.22: interior of the 1030–1190 cluster.
No variable is perched on a sharp peak; the predicted strength should stay ≈1050–1190 MPa throughout.

**Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=500, DT=855, Dt=16, QmT=140, TT=165, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.21, Si=0.30, Mn=0.65, P=0.012, S=0.014, Ni=1.65, Cr=0.58, Cu=0.10, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=690, dA=0.05, dB=0.005, dC=0.004**
